newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN DEBT IN BETTER SHAPE BUT GAINS SEEN LIMITED.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN DEBT IN BETTER SHAPE BUT GAINS SEEN LIMITED.

text.p: German debt prices will strive to maintain higher levels on Thursday after strength in U.S. Treasuries jolted the market back into a more positive mood.

But after a day spent entirely in negative ground on Wednesday and nervousness about the threat of possible monetary moves by the Bundesbank, analysts said the market was unlikely to make significant headway.
A fresh set of inflation data is also due from the U.S., another factor likely to keep prices gaisn in Bunds limited.
By 0724 GMT, the September DTB Bund future was trading 19 basis points higher on the day at 102.15.
"Any move higher is likely to find tough resistance from the 102.30/34 area," analysts at MMS International said in a morning note.
The short end of the market, as on Wednesday, is likely to remain under pressure as speculation about a possible repo rate rise continues ahead of the next repurschase agreement due on Tuesday.
Analysts at DMG Futures and and Options in Frankfurt said that with this in mind, investors should favour curve flattening trade in the coming sessions.
July U.S. consumer prices are due at 1230 GMT, forecast up 0.2 percent on the month versus 0.1 percent in June.
The numbers will be just one set in a flurry of releases due this session, including business inventories, capacity utilisation, real earnings and weekly money supply data.
If the data give Treasuries a lift, economists said Bunds would benefit too, but were unlikely to keep pace.
On Wednesday, Bunds underperformed the U.S. market, slimming the 10-year yield gap to 78 basis points by the close. That underperformance was set to continue this session, analysts said.
